sentences.text: Jade Pritchard is the mother of Lily and Mason.
Lily is eight months old.
The visit is part of Lily's eight-month review.
The health visitor is Claire Dunmore.
The health visitor (Claire Dunmore) is conducting a health visit with Jade Pritchard.
Lily's weight at last review was 7.9 kilos.
Lily's current weight is 8.4 kilos.
Lily is following her growth line.
Lily is on a weaning diet of porridge in the morning and mashed vegetables at dinner.
Lily still drinks four bottles per day.
Each bottle is seven ounces.
Lily does not always finish the night bottle.
Lily is trying finger foods such as bits of toast and banana.
Lily gags when eating finger foods, which concerns the mother.
The health visitor explains that gagging is normal and choking is different (silent), and provides a leaflet on choking.
Lily sleeps around seven in the evening and wakes once around three for a bottle.
Mason sleeps more than Lily, and the mother admits Mason is worse than Lily in terms of sleep patterns.
Dean Pritchard (father) works on lorries, Monday to Friday, and returns on weekends.
The mother is alone during the week with the children.
The mother's mother (grandmother) helps out on Tuesdays with Mason.
Mason has fifteen hours of childcare at Little Acorns per week.
The mother reports financial strain, describing the household as 'tight'.
The household receives Universal Credit and money from Dean.
Electricity costs have increased significantly and the household is on a key meter.
The health visitor provides the number for the Harbridge Energy Fund, which offers top-ups.
The mother reports being 'alright' but tired and bored in the evenings.
The mother drinks a bottle of wine every night, most nights, when the children are in bed.
The mother drinks a standard bottle of 75 centilitres from the Co-op.
The mother starts drinking around eight o'clock when the children are in bed.
The mother smokes a small amount of cannabis (weed) a couple of nights a week, only when the children are in bed, never in front of them.
